Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity sizing for Atlas AI POC — initial modeling

Olga / Rafael / Alex,

I ran a quick capacity model based on the stated constraints. Summary first, then the assumptions and math (attached workbook: atlasai_tps_modeling.xlsx).

Short recommendation (POC-level):
- Start Dedicated slab: 8 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool). This provides a steady-state headroom for current 5M tokens/day and ~50% buffer for short spikes.
- Autoscale / burst to: 12 GPUs for up to ~30 minutes during high marketing bursts (can be governed by quota/burst policy).
- Canary/rollout: start with one GPU in the pool pinned to the model, route 10% traffic through canary for 48 hours, then ramp.

Key assumptions and derivation:
- Model throughput baseline: redwood-open-7b-quant ~3,200 tokens/sec per GPU at typical 400-token request size (measured with our internal perf harness at 32 batch). This number drops as response length grows because KV cache and attention passes scale with sequence length; for 2k-token responses we estimate ~1,200 tokens/sec per GPU.
- Average tokens per request assumption: 400 (Atlas provided).
- Steady tokens/day -> per-second avg: 5,000,000 / 86,400 ≈ 58 tokens/sec average. That is low because bursts dominate — we shape sizing on TPS during peak windows.
- Peak sustained: 1,200 req/min = 20 req/sec. At avg 400 tokens = 8,000 tokens/sec.
- Concurrency effect: with batching we can reach close to per-GPU throughput, but latency SLO of 300ms at 2k tokens constrains batch sizes. For tight 95th latency at 2k tokens we use the 1,200 tokens/sec per GPU estimate.

Capacity math for peak SLO fit (95th):
- Required tokens/sec at worst-case peak = 8,000 tps (avg 400 tokens).
- If many requests are 2k tokens, worst-case tokens/sec spike could be 4x → 32,000 tps.
- Using conservative 1,200 tps per GPU for 2k-token case: GPUs needed = ceil(32,000 / 1,200) ≈ 27 GPUs.
- For expected mixed distribution (20% 2k, 80% 400) effective tokens/sec per GPU ~2,400. Then GPUs needed for 8,000 tps ≈ ceil(8,000/2,400) = 4 GPUs; add 50% headroom → 6 GPUs.

What this means practically:
- If Atlas sees many 2k responses during spikes, commit should be sized at ~24-30 GPUs to maintain 95th <= 300ms.
- If distribution stays mostly 400-token responses, a much smaller pool (6-10 GPUs) will meet SLOs with headroom.

Recommendation for procurement:
- Offer Tier A (conservative): 24 GPU commit, supports up to sustained high-length spikes with 1020% margin.
- Offer Tier B (economical): 8 GPU commit + 12-GPU burst pool (on-demand/enterprise burst) and autoscaling policy, with documented fallback to a slightly lower-latency-optimized model for extreme spikes.

I attached the spreadsheet with a worksheet that lets you swap avg tokens/request and percent of long responses to see GPU need.
